newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Dexia CC drops on issue news, arbitrage.
newsitem.headline: Dexia CC drops on issue news, arbitrage.

text.p: Shares in Belgian bank Dexia CC fell by over one percent in active trade on Thursday morning on surprise news of a new stock offering by its controlling shareholder and as a result of arbitrage against shares in French partner bank Dexia CLF.
By 0920 GMT Dexia CC shares were down 45 Belgian francs, or 1.24 percent, at 3,580 francs. In Paris Dexia CLF shares were up seven French francs at 559 francs (3,420 Belgian francs).

Belgium's towns and municipalities, which own 65.5 percent of Dexia CC, said late on Wednesday they would sell up to 15.5 percent more of their holding in a global offering in the second quarter of 1997, probably in June.
Dealers said that the news took the market by surprise, but was not the only factor hitting the share.

"Since Dexia CC was issued there has always been a premium of the Belgian share over the French one. It was nearly nine percent on Monday and now it's reducing," said Bernard du Parc, head trader at brokerage BBL/Vermeulen Raemdonck.
Given there was still a premium despite the stock issue news, Dexia CC could fall further, he added.
Generale Bank said in an investor note on the stock issue news that it rated Dexia CC a hold for the time being.

It noted the additional shares would increase liquidity in Dexia CC and increase the chance the stock will enter the Bel-20 share index in December when the bourse carries out its annual review of the Bel-20's composition.
